text:
The file on Detective Howard’s desk was not just evidence; it was a betrayal wrapped in paper. He stared at the photograph, his hand trembling slightly as he reached for the apple on his desk—a simple, red fruit that had been his comfort for thirty years. The color of the apple matched the flush of shame rising in his cheeks.

Howard looked at the photo again. It showed his partner, Miller, handing over a briefcase to a known crime lord. The timing was perfect, the location undeniable. But the loyalty Howard had felt for decades warred with the duty he was about to retire from. If he reported this, he destroyed the man who had been his brother in arms. If he didn’t, he betrayed the badge he was about to hang up.

He took a bite of the apple. The crisp sound echoed in the silent office, loud as a gunshot. The red juice stained his fingers, looking suspiciously like blood. He had to choose. The color of the fruit was a reminder of the truth: it was either red or it wasn’t. There was no gray area in justice, only the stark, bloody contrast of right and wrong. Howard closed the file, the weight of the decision pressing down on him like a physical force.
